normal_spacing_scope: Original abs remains first. Only finite positive normal magnitudes below maxfinite use the exact exponent-derived normal binary64 ULP. All zero/subnormal/maxfinite/nonfinite cases retain the original nextafter expression and its exception/errno behavior. Root independently reviews/tests linked-libm FEnv/errno equivalence before runtime admission.
copy_scope: Complete active memcpy retained at all nine sites. Inactive host rows are cleared only while that Stage.program_uploaded is false. Header/program host suffix, every consumed upload byte, device state, authorized host reads and refusal/rollback behavior are unchanged. Inactive unconsumed host bytes may differ after a successful full upload.

upload_wire_invariant.false: Full serialization follows unchanged inactive clear plus full active memcpy. Failed writes leave the flag false, so a smaller retry clears newly inactive rows before its next full write; any partial-write behavior receives the same wire bytes and call sequence.
upload_wire_invariant.true: Successful full upload already installed the immutable program tail. Every later serialization is exactly header plus active rows; each active row is fully copied before upload, including newly active rows after growth. Skipped inactive host bytes never enter those uploads. A later dispatch/read/decode/timing failure does not invalidate the completed upload.
upload_wire_invariant.paired_endpoint_dense: The two Stage flags remain independent. Endpoint write success followed by Dense write failure leaves Endpoint true and Dense false, exactly as before; write order, early returns and each subsequent serialized range are unchanged.
upload_wire_invariant.preparation_and_reset: Preparation writes only device header zero/restored capacity and never changes the host input or uploaded-program flag. ResetStatistics changes neither. Cancellation and errors retain original ordering and flag lifetime.
upload_wire_invariant.stage_seven_host_reader: Step invalidates every issued bit before validation/staging. Only successfully decoded active result rows may be issued; authorization checks matching issuer/generation/row and issued before reading that transport input row. No inactive stale host tail is consumed.
